thread:
Alex Chen: Ran a long-context perf run (100k tokens) across hosted/dedicated/private. Seeing sustained RSS growth on Dedicated after ~30k tokens, but hosted looks stable. :confused:
Priya Rao: curious — same model + quantization/kv config?
Alex Chen: yep, same model binary + int8 q config. Only difference was allocator flags and node kernel (dedicated = cloud image w/ older kernel).
Michael Ortega: can you paste the profiler output?
Alex Chen: sure, gist: ```
vmstat shows high majflt growth, /proc/slabinfo shows increasing 'kv_entry' slab partials, page reclaim spikes
perf top -> page_table_fault and __split_huge_page hot on dedicated
```
Noah Patel: that smells like hugepage split + slab fragmentation. On our on-prem images we enable hugetlb for perf but dedicated images might not match.
Priya Rao: hosted uses AWS Nitro + kernel 6.x with transparent hugepages off by default, if dedicated uses older kernel it may eagerly split pages under certain mmap patterns.
Alex Chen: repro strategy I ran: pinned a single model instance and sent long seq streaming to exhaust KV reuse; ded shows incremental growth even after GC windows.
Michael Ortega: did you disable prefix caching? Could be KV reuse policy interacting with eviction frequency.
Alex Chen: prefix cache disabled for the test; behavior persists. Also saw more small slabs left behind on dedicated: fragmentation increases memory footprint even though active KV count stable.
Noah Patel: I can spin a dedicated node with newer kernel + same allocator flags and compare. Also try jemalloc opt: background_thread toggled?
Alex Chen: jemalloc background_thread=1 reduced peak by ~6% but didn't fix growth slope. Turning off transparent hugepage on dedicated fixed the split_hot path in perf and growth stabilized.
Priya Rao: aha — so kernel THP/hugepage policy difference is the likely root cause. That would explain hosted vs dedicated delta without changing runtime code.
Michael Ortega: for Private (on-prem) we also saw odd fragmentation but from different cause: GPU memory allocator pinned host vma alignments which forced non-2MB mappings for KV pages. Leads to mix of page sizes and slab fragmentation.
Noah Patel: summary: three coupling issues — kernel THP policy (dedicated), allocator background threading (tunable), and vma alignment on on-prem (private). All manifest as KV slab partials and RSS growth on long-context workloads.
Alex Chen: suggested mitigation: add runtime guard to detect hugepage splits (tracepoint) and auto-disable THP/adjust MADV flags for KV mmaps; also emit metric kv.slab_partial_ratio per model_shard.
Priya Rao: +1 on metric. Also a rollout plan: try kernel flag change on a small dedicated pool, run long-context canary (48h) and compare slab_partial_ratio and majflt rate.
Michael Ortega: create an infra ticket for dedicated images to sync kernel + default madvise flags. I'll own that.
Noah Patel: I'll prototype the runtime tracepoint and metric PR (small change). Alex can run canary jobs and attach flamegraphs.
Alex Chen: posted canary results to the canary channel when ready. For now: repro commands below — runs on a single GPU instance, script streams tokens to model endpoint:
```
# run repro
python tools/long_context_stream.py --addr http://dedicated-node:8080 --seq-len 100000 --batch 1 --duration 4h
# collect vmstats
watch -n 10 "cat /proc/vmstat | egrep 'pgmajfault|pgfault'"
perf record -a -g -- sleep 300; perf report
```
Priya Rao: nice. One more ask: add a small note in the release notes for dedicated customers — we are toggling madvise/hugepage policy to stabilize long-context workloads. Need comms before infra change.
deploy-bot: Deployed image 'dedicated-2026-03-17-kernel-6.4' to pool small-dedicated-1 (canary) — rollout paused.
Michael Ortega: thanks, will validate. If canary looks good we'll schedule rollout and include KB entry on kernel flags + why it matters. :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: assigning follow-ups: infra ticket #INF-1209 (Michael), runtime metrics PR (Noah), canary runs (Alex). Will update this thread with links. :eyes:
